messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: EIGEN_NO_DEBUG rabbit hole (LDLT, factor_U, append_col/row, ...)
parts:
At some point, our code diverged from being compatible with
Eigen debugging. The develop branch only passes tests
if -DEIGEN_NO_DEBUG is part of CFLAGS.

Can someone explain why this restriction got added to the code? I'd
like to make sure it's absolutely necessary. I don't think we have the
resources to maintain two versions of the code, but I hate to cut
off the option of running with range checks.

The specific problem I'm having is that it's very very useful for
debugging to run without disabling Eigen's debugging.



Daniel and I have started to fix these issues on:

bugfix/issue-904-eigen-assert-bugs

The LDLT test code indicated it wouldn't run otherwise.

append_row and append_col had broken tests with mismatches sizes
which must have only run by overwriting memory without segfaulting,
but there's no indication of why. I ifdefed out the test.

There are lots of these cases, but some of them may be dependent
on others.

I'd like to fix all of these and where it's not possible, indicate
why in the function and make sure the test code has an #ifdef so
I can run tests without disabling the debug flag.

- Bob

We decided to do all the range-checking in Stan code, so the range-checking in Eigen was redundant. But that meant we can't turn off range-checking in the Stan code even when we want to.

Daniel and I have started to fix these issues on:

  bugfix/issue-904-eigen-assert-bugs

The LDLT test code indicated it wouldn't run otherwise.

I pushed a fix into that branch. The test made no sense.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: EIGEN_NO_DEBUG rabbit hole (LDLT, factor_U, append_col/row, ...)
parts:
On Wednesday, August 27, 2014 12:37:12 AM UTC-4, Ben Goodrich wrote:
We seem to have another failure in BFGS update. I'll look at it.

This seems to be a more serious problem. In

src/stan/optimization/bfgs_update.hpp

      inline void search_direction(VectorT &pk, const VectorT &gk) const {
        pk.noalias() = -(_Hk*gk);
      }

    private:
      HessianT _Hk;

the search_direction method is getting called when _Hk is uninitialized, meaning that it is a 0x0 matrix. So, with asserts disabled, it allows _Hk*gk to happen when gk is of length K > 0.

The real problem seems to be the default template thing:

 namespace stan {
   namespace optimization {
     template<typename Scalar = double,
-             int DimAtCompile = Eigen::Dynamic>
+             int DimAtCompile = -1>
     class BFGSUpdate_HInv {


since Eigen::Dynamic is an alias for zero. Changing it to -1 might break some stuff, but it should be safe.

We should unit-test with Eigen asserts on but compile users' models with them off.

Ben

I agree that we should use the debug mode for tests then turn
it off at run time. The reason is that goal is to catch programming
mistakes, not run-time errors. If the latter happen, they're
also programming mistakes.

Yes, Eigen::Dynamic is -1, but if you call the default no-arg
constructor you get a 0 x 0 matrix. You can then assign different
dimensionality matrices to it.

- Bob
